text: Minimum credit score: conventional fixed-rate loans require a minimum representative credit score of 620. Adjustable-rate loans require a minimum score of 640.
Debt-to-income ratio: the maximum total DTI is 45% for manually underwritten loans. Loans approved through automated underwriting may go up to 50% DTI with compensating factors.
Loan-to-value limits: the maximum LTV for a primary residence purchase is 97% for first-time homebuyers and 95% for all other borrowers. Cash-out refinances are capped at 80% LTV.
Mortgage insurance: private mortgage insurance is required when LTV exceeds 80%. Borrowers may request cancellation once the principal balance reaches 80% of the original property value.
Reserves: investment property purchases require six months of principal, interest, taxes and insurance in reserves. Primary residences with a DTI above 45% require two months of reserves.
Self-employed income: self-employed borrowers must document two years of personal and business tax returns. Income that declined more than 20% year over year must be explained in writing.
Gift funds: gift funds from a relative are acceptable for a primary residence down payment and require a signed gift letter stating that no repayment is expected.
Appraisals: an appraisal is valid for 120 days from the effective date. A recertification of value may extend validity to 12 months.
Occupancy: borrowers must occupy a primary residence within 60 days of closing and intend to live there for at least one year.
Condominiums: a condo project must have no more than 15% of units that are 60 or more days delinquent on HOA dues. No single entity may own more than 20% of the units.
Payment history: a borrower with a mortgage payment 30 days late within the last 12 months is ineligible for a cash-out refinance.
Bankruptcy waiting period: a Chapter 7 bankruptcy requires a four-year waiting period from the discharge date. A Chapter 13 bankruptcy requires two years from the discharge date.
